title: How the rules may apply
text_content:
This is based only on the facts you confirmed. It is not a decision; your bank assesses which rules apply.

Bank account payments (S$4,850): Likely covered by the SRF
- This looks like the kind of phishing scam the SRF covers: a digital message impersonating an organisation, details entered on a fake website or app, and payments you did not intend.

Because the scam message came by SMS, your mobile operator may be responsible if your bank met all its duties and the operator did not meet its own. Your bank assesses this; disagreements about the operator go to IMDA in writing, not to FIDReC.

Sources: MAS/IMDA Guidelines on Shared Responsibility Framework (effective 16 Dec 2024); MAS E-Payments User Protection Guidelines.

Terms used:
- SRF: the Shared Responsibility Framework, under which banks and mobile operators may share losses from certain phishing scams.
- IMDA: the Infocomm Media Development Authority, which regulates mobile operators.
- FIDReC: the Financial Industry Disputes Resolution Centre, which resolves disputes between consumers and financial institutions.

title: Free evaluation summary
text_content: You experienced a phishing scam through SMS on 3 Mar 2026. You entered your credentials on a fake website or app, which led to unauthorized transactions from your bank account. On the same day, three transactions were made to an account ending in 0001, totaling S$4,850. You discovered the scam on 4 Mar 2026, and reported it to Harbourline Bank the same day. You also sent a written complaint on 6 Mar 2026. The bank provided a case reference number, SAMPLE-HB-0001, and later issued a final reply on 20 Apr 2026, rejecting your claim. You told us that you reported the incident to the police on 4 Mar 2026, and received a police report number, SAMPLE-POL-0001. No amount has been recovered or offered to you as compensation.
